Market Intelligence Briefing
subheadings: 🇺🇸 United States  Mixed  on hold / hawkish handover
🇪🇺 European Union  Bullish  on hold / strong-euro watch
🇨🇳 China  Mixed  easing bias / weak demand
🇯🇵 Japan  Bullish  gradual hikes / election mandate
🇵🇱 Poland  Bullish  easing bias / strong growth
🧮 Earnings Pattern — What the Market Pays For
Proof beats promise: the market pays for AI cash returns and scarcity, and sells capex and disruption risk
🔍 Underowned Themes — Active on X, Underweight in Portfolios
China property and insurers: Beijing has started to repair the balance sheet
Japanese banks: a BOJ worried about falling behind the curve
Bitcoin at a 2025-tariff-shock low: a liquidity and Fed-chair problem, not a crypto-specific one
Dollar bounce, bear steepener, open credit markets: liquidity is fine, duration is not
🔮 Anticipatory Positioning — Markets Pricing In Future Events
Warsh at the Fed: a hawkish regime change priced in one session
Japan's Feb. 8 election: a landslide is the base case
$PLTR  AI software the market must re-separate from SaaS  ↑
$LLY  Medicare coverage and the obesity pill  ↑
$AMD  MI450 timing risk into the print  ↓
Silver / SLV  "the meme metal after a record crash"
Strategy / MSTR and BitMine / BMNR  "leveraged crypto proxies in a drawdown"
body: Monday, February 02 2026 — Macro · Sectors · Flows · Crypto

Macro Stance: Growth is not the problem: third-quarter GDP rose 4.4%, the fastest in two years, and the Fed held rates while upgrading its view of the economy. Inflation is: producer prices posted their biggest gain in five months as firms passed on tariffs. Households feel worse than the data, with confidence at its lowest since 2014 — a K-shaped economy that keeps the Fed on hold rather than easing.

Rates & Curve: The 2Y closed at 3.52% and the 10Y at 4.26%, a 74 bps 10Y−2Y spread; over 20 observations the 2Y rose 5 bps and the 10Y 8 bps, a bear steepening (both up, 10Y up more) that leaves the curve moderately steep, approaching the long-run average (US Treasury, prior close 2026-01-30). The S&P 500 closed at 6,939.03, up 1.37% over 20 sessions, with the VIX at 17.44 and the DXY up 0.74% in the prior session to 96.99 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-01-30).

New / Most Important: The Fed-chair pick was read as hawkish — traders see Kevin Warsh as the tougher choice — and the reaction was violent: gold fell 10.78% and silver 31.35% in the prior session while the dollar index rose 0.74% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-01-30). Confirmation is not a formality, since Senator Tillis will oppose the nominee until the Powell probe is resolved.

Playbook ✓: Stay long US equities but short duration: own the bear-steepening winners (energy, industrial capex, large banks), underweight TLT, and hedge the hawkish-chair tail with VIX calls while the VIX sits at 17.44 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-01-30). Flip toward duration only if the jobs data Reuters flags alongside a heavy earnings week disappoint, or if Warsh signals near-term cuts.

Macro Stance: Bullish. The euro-zone economy unexpectedly grew 0.3% in the fourth quarter, and a Bloomberg poll has the ECB locked on hold as calls for hikes fade — neutral policy while growth surprises upward. The STOXX 600 rose 3.07% over 20 sessions versus 1.37% for the S&P 500, with the Euro Stoxx 50 at 5,947.81 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-01-30).

Activity & Inflation: Germany is the weak link: unemployment hit a 12-year high and Merz now calls the economy his main focus. The DAX was flat over 20 sessions and the CAC 40 fell 0.84%, against a 3.07% gain for the STOXX 600 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-01-30) — banks and the periphery are doing the work, not the core exporters.

New / Most Important: The euro's rally to $1.20 is now the ECB's headache: a stronger currency imports disinflation and squeezes exporters, so the next policy debate is about cutting, not hiking. EUR/USD closed at 1.1966, up 1.83% over 20 sessions, and GBP/USD at 1.3806 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-01-30).

Playbook ✓: Own domestic euro-area cyclicals and banks and underweight euro-earning exporters (autos, luxury) while EUR/USD holds near 1.1966 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-01-30). Switch toward Bunds if January inflation undershoots and ECB officials start citing the euro's strength as a reason to cut.

Macro Stance: Mixed. Fourth-quarter growth slowed to 4.5%, the weakest in nearly three years, as consumption missed forecasts. Beijing's response is targeted rather than broad — property-rule relief, insurer recapitalisation, a stronger-yuan agenda — which supports equity sentiment more than it fixes household demand.

PMIs & Activity: The official manufacturing PMI dropped to 49.3 in January, back below the 50 line. The feed carries no fresh non-manufacturing or industrial-output print beyond that, so the read is simple: factories are not yet feeling the policy shift. A turn needs the PMI back above 50 and new orders lifting after the Lunar New Year.

Credit Impulse: The feed carries no fresh January credit print; the latest, from mid-January, showed new loans shrinking to the least since 2018 as demand weakened. Policy is working on plumbing rather than volume — Beijing plans $29 billion of special bonds to recapitalise insurers. A rebound in January new loans and social financing would be the first sign that the impulse is turning.

Property: Beijing reportedly dropped the rules that sparked the property crisis, and developer shares surged. The damage is still surfacing: Vanke warned its 2025 loss may have widened to $11.8 billion. Relief on leverage rules helps surviving developers fund themselves, not end demand — the test is whether sales and prices stabilise in the spring selling season.

Fiscal, Policy & Trade: China logged its first fiscal revenue drop since 2020 on the property slump and weak consumption — the budget is constraining, not cushioning. The external front is about the currency: Xi called for the renminbi to attain global reserve-currency status, a goal that implies tolerating a stronger yuan and more open capital markets. That is a currency story for portfolio flows, not a fiscal impulse for households.

Markets & Flows: The Hang Seng closed at 27,387.11, down 2.08% in the prior session but up 3.98% over 20 sessions, and the Shanghai Composite ended at 4,117.95, up 3.76% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-01-30). ASHR rose 1.8% and KWEB 3.91% over 20 sessions, while USD/CNY fell 0.69% to 6.9480 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-01-30); the yuan hit a 32-month high earlier in the week as the PBOC strengthened its guidance.

New / Most Important: The signal is the policy mix, not the data: leverage rules for developers eased, insurers are being recapitalised and the yuan is being guided higher. That favours financials and Hong Kong-listed platforms over exporters, while the weak PMI keeps pressure on Beijing to add direct demand support.

Playbook ✓: Own China through Hong Kong financials and internet (FXI, KWEB) on dips, treat developer rallies as trades until Vanke's restructuring settles, and avoid exporters exposed to a firmer yuan. Upgrade to Bullish if January credit data rebound and the PMI returns above 50; cut if USD/CNY reverses its 0.69% 20-session decline (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-01-30). ⚠ Divergence: Xi wants a strong, reserve-grade currency and the yuan hit a 32-month high days ago, yet the PMI is in contraction at 49.3 — currency strength is tightening conditions just as domestic demand needs relief.

Macro Stance: Bullish. Polls show Takaichi's party poised for a landslide in the Feb. 8 Lower House vote, and the BOJ's January summary shows members debating the risk of falling behind the curve on inflation. A strong mandate plus a central bank leaning toward normalisation is good for domestic earnings and for banks.

Activity & Currency: USD/JPY closed at 153.16, down 2.28% over 20 sessions and 3.37% over five as the yen rallied, while the Nikkei 225 ended at 53,322.85, up 5.53% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-01-30). Equities absorbed a stronger yen, which says the rally is domestic and financial rather than export-led.

Playbook ✓: Own domestic financials and reflation plays into the vote and hedge exporters' yen exposure. Cut the call if the LDP misses a majority, or if a consumption-tax suspension, which the finance minister says Tokyo is carefully considering, reignites a selloff in long-dated JGBs.

Macro Stance: Bearish for domestic equities. Inflation jumped to 3.8%, CBA economists expect the cash rate to rise to 3.85%, and the hike is expected at Tuesday's meeting. A central bank tightening against the global trend raises the discount rate for the whole market.

Demand & Financing: AUD/USD closed at 0.7047, up 5.53% over 20 sessions, while the ASX 200 ended at 8,869.10, up only 1.78% and down 1.08% in the prior session (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-01-30). A currency outrunning the index is an earnings headwind for offshore earners and a funding-cost squeeze for mortgaged households.

Playbook ✓: Underweight rate-sensitive ASX sectors and AUD-earning exporters, keep long AUD/USD through the decision, and prefer bank margins to housing-linked names. Reverse if the RBA holds instead of moving to 3.85% — that would push AUD back toward 0.6678, its level 20 sessions earlier (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-01-30).

Monetary & Activity: GDP grew 3.6% in 2025, according to GUS data reported by Rzeczpospolita, and MPC member Kotecki said a rate cut could come as early as February — easing into strong growth, the best mix for domestic equities. With the zloty firm, imported inflation is not the constraint on the council.

FX & Markets: USD/PLN closed at 3.5139, down 1.98% over 20 sessions, with EUR/PLN at 4.2041; EPOL rose 6.82% and the WIG20TR ETF 5.69% over 20 sessions, led by PGE (+14.04%), Orlen (+12.33%) and PKO BP (+8.71%), while KGHM fell 10.7% and CD Projekt 8.0% in the prior session (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-01-30). The WIG20 hit its highest level in 18 years; CD Projekt's drop came on the day videogame stocks slid on Google's AI world-builder.

Companies: KGHM's CEO was dismissed and a successor named in what Business Insider Polska called an earthquake, just as silver and copper reversed. LPP will pay a record dividend of at least 800 zł per share, and PKO BP and PZU, up 8.71% and 5.0% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-01-30), remain the income core of the index.

Security & New Development: Poland signed off on a €3.5 billion 'breakthrough' anti-drone defence system, the clearest sign that defence spending is now a domestic investment theme. Combined with a possible February cut, fiscal and monetary policy are both leaning pro-growth.

Playbook ✓: Own PKO BP and PGE and keep zloty exposure unhedged while EUR/PLN holds near 4.20 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-01-30); trim KGHM until governance settles. ⚠ Divergence: the WIG20 sits at an 18-year high while KGHM lost its CEO and fell 10.7% in a day (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-01-30) — political risk at state champions has not been priced out.

Narrative: Consensus still treats tech as one AI trade, but the tape split it: XLK was flat over 20 sessions (-0.06%) while MSFT fell 11.03%, ORCL 15.56% and PLTR 17.53% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-01-30). The market is separating owners of scarce AI capacity from seat-based software it fears AI will disrupt.

Reported: Microsoft lost $357 billion of market value as the stock plunged the most since 2020, with slowing cloud growth set against huge AI spending. IBM, by contrast, jumped 8% on its beat, and AAPL gained 4.61% over five sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-01-30).

EPS Upside Watch: Palantir reports on Feb. 2 after a 17.53% slide over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-01-30), so the bar has been lowered for an AI-revenue name. In hardware, the memory squeeze that lifts suppliers is a cost for device makers — upside sits with storage and memory vendors, not assemblers.

⚡ Breaking Convention: IBM's 8% jump shows the 'AI eats software' trade is too blunt: a legacy vendor was rewarded because AI is lifting its software demand. If AI attach shows up in renewals, the most-hated SaaS names become the cheapest AI beneficiaries.

Narrative: Communication services is where AI spending is already being paid for: XLC rose 2.0% and META 8.55% over 20 sessions while XLK went nowhere and NFLX fell 10.95% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-01-30). Platforms with ad engines can fund capex from revenue, which is exactly what investors now demand.

Reported: Meta jumped 10% on a stronger-than-expected revenue forecast, proof that a big AI budget is forgiven when the top line accelerates with it. META gave back 2.95% in the prior session as the Nasdaq 100 fell 1.28% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-01-30).

EPS Upside Watch: Alphabet headlines the busiest week of the reporting period alongside Amazon. GOOGL rose 7.99% over 20 sessions to 338.00 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-01-30); a cloud acceleration that matches Meta's revenue story would carry the whole sector.

⚡ Breaking Convention: Google's AI is destroying value inside its own sector: videogame stocks slid on its model that turns prompts into playable worlds. XLC is a bet on the AI platforms, not on content owners — underweight gaming and streaming.

Narrative: Financials lagged — XLF fell 2.43% and JPM 5.07% over 20 sessions while GS rose 6.42% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-01-30). The driver that matters now is the Fed pick: Warsh is likely to boost Wall Street rule easing, and a bear-steepening curve widens lending margins.

Reported: Visa beat first-quarter estimates as holiday sales boosted payment volumes — card-network spending is intact. BAC rose 2.86% and JPM 2.74% over five sessions as the banks stabilised (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-01-30).

EPS Upside Watch: Capital-markets franchises: US high-grade bond sales topped $200 billion in a record yearly start, feeding underwriting fees at GS and the money-centre banks. Deregulation under a new chair is an estimate driver not yet in consensus numbers.

⚡ Breaking Convention: The risk sits next to the banks: Bloomberg warns private credit is headed for a software shock — the same AI-disruption fear that crushed software stocks now threatens loans to software companies. Own the money-centre banks, avoid BDCs concentrated in software lending.

Narrative: Energy is the clearest trend of the year: XLE rose 14.18% over 20 sessions as Brent climbed 16.17% to 70.69 and WTI 13.57% to 65.21 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-01-30). Iran is the driver — oil surged to a five-month high on worries the US could attack.

Reported: Exxon beat as Permian and Guyana fields took output to a 40-year high; XOM rose 17.5% and CVX 16.07% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-01-30). Volume growth, not price, carried the majors' quarter.

EPS Upside Watch: Gas-weighted producers: Henry Hub is still up 18.12% over 20 sessions despite a 17.46% five-session drop (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-01-30), so first-quarter realised prices should beat estimates set before the cold snap. Producers combining record volumes with higher spot prices carry the cleanest upside.

⚡ Breaking Convention: The premium is fragile: Brent's 20-session gain rests on an Iran attack that has not happened, and the gas market shows how fast a premium unwinds — Henry Hub lost 17.46% in five sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-01-30). Hold producers with volume growth, not crude itself.

Narrative: Industrials have become an AI-power trade: XLI rose 6.65% and CAT 14.75% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-01-30), and NERC forecasts peak demand rising 24% on new data-centre loads. Turbines, gensets and grid gear are the bottleneck, which gives their makers pricing power that a soft factory cycle cannot erode.

Reported: Caterpillar jumped as power-generation demand made it a surprise AI play, and GE Vernova's fourth-quarter gas-turbine orders surged 74%. GE rose 2.65% in the prior session while BA fell 7.31% over five (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-01-30).

EPS Upside Watch: Power-generation suppliers: a 74% jump in turbine orders converts into revenue over several years, so backlog-driven upside persists even if the AI capex debate cools. Defence primes with European order books are the second leg.

⚡ Breaking Convention: The cycle under the rally is weak: the December ISM manufacturing PMI was 47.9%. XLI is pricing capex, not a cyclical recovery — own power and defence, not short-cycle machinery that needs a manufacturing upturn.

Narrative: Discretionary is K-shaped: XLY rose 1.47% over 20 sessions while TSLA fell 4.29%, NKE 2.98% and HD rose 8.86% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-01-30). Confidence at its lowest since 2014 has not yet shown up in housing-linked names.

Reported: GM hit an all-time high on upbeat results and a buyback, with its CFO calling the stock undervalued — trucks and capital returns beat EV ambition. TSLA rose 3.32% in the prior session but is down 4.15% over five (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-01-30).

EPS Upside Watch: Amazon reports in the busiest week of the season; AMZN is up 3.67% over 20 sessions at 239.30 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-01-30). AWS acceleration plus retail margin discipline is the set-up for a beat, and a modest 20-session gain leaves room for a positive reaction.

⚡ Breaking Convention: Sentiment and spending have decoupled: confidence sits at a 2014 low while the S&P 500 is 1.37% higher over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-01-30). The sector's bigger risk is a hawkish Fed and higher real rates, not the shopper.

Narrative: Staples are the hiding place: XLP rose 7.51% over 20 sessions and 1.68% in the prior session, with WMT up 6.94% and COST 9.03% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-01-30). A hawkish Fed pick and crowded tech positioning keep the rotation into defensives alive.

Reported: Procter & Gamble missed revenue estimates on slower US growth — the sector rally is not about volumes. The winners are price-makers with traffic, Walmart and Costco, not the branded-goods makers.

EPS Upside Watch: Walmart and Costco: membership and grocery traffic hold up in a K-shaped economy, and both have outpaced the S&P 500's 1.37% 20-session gain (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-01-30). Upside comes from mix — services and membership fees — not from price.

⚡ Breaking Convention: P&G's miss says US demand for branded staples is slowing even as the group re-rates. If defensives are bid only for safety, a risk-on turn after strong Big Tech prints would hit XLP first.

Narrative: Healthcare is the policy loser: XLV was flat over 20 sessions (-0.04%) while UNH fell 19.46% over five sessions and LLY 3.49% over 20 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-01-30). Medicare rates and drug-price politics are compressing the multiples of the sector's biggest names.

Reported: UnitedHealth forecast its first revenue drop in nearly four decades and the shares plunged; managed care now trades like a regulated utility with negative growth. UNH closed at 286.93 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-01-30).

EPS Upside Watch: Obesity drugs: Lilly's CEO says Medicare coverage could change the game for the pill launch, and Lilly is among the week's reporters. Volume from new coverage is the one clear estimate upside in the sector.

⚡ Breaking Convention: Lilly is a policy winner in a policy-loser sector: Medicare coverage expands the market even as negotiation squeezes legacy drugs. Pair long LLY against managed care until UNH proves a revenue floor.

Narrative: Materials were January's winner and are now the unwind: XLB is still up 8.64% over 20 sessions, but gold fell 10.78%, silver 31.35% and copper 4.51% in the prior session, with NEM down 11.49% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-01-30). The Warsh pick punctured the debasement trade.

Reported: Dow will cut 4,500 jobs and forecast weak revenue amid sluggish demand — chemicals have no AI tailwind. FCX fell 7.52% in the prior session but remains up 18.59% over 20 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-01-30).

EPS Upside Watch: Copper producers: copper soared past $14,500 a ton before the retreat, and the front month at 5.90 is still up 4.74% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-01-30). Quarterly realised prices should run ahead of estimates set before the spike.

⚡ Breaking Convention: Copper fell far less than gold and silver in the prior session (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-01-30): the AI data-centre and grid metal is decoupling from the precious-metals unwind. After a run past $14,500, own FCX over gold miners.

Narrative: REITs are fighting the curve: XLRE rose 2.68% over 20 sessions while the 10Y rose 8 bps to 4.26% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-01-30; US Treasury, prior close 2026-01-30). A hawkish Fed chair pick limits the rate relief the sector needs.

Reported: Keppel DC REIT's second-half DPU rose 7.1% on acquisitions and strong portfolio reversion — data-centre landlords are delivering where office and housing-linked REITs are not. XLRE itself closed at 41.43, up 0.15% in the prior session (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-01-30).

EPS Upside Watch: Data-centre landlords: the Keppel result shows rent reversion running with AI demand, and NERC's 24% peak-demand forecast says the scarce asset is powered land. Prefer data-centre and tower REITs within XLRE.

⚡ Breaking Convention: Bear steepening is the enemy, but the 2Y fell 8 bps over five observations (US Treasury, prior close 2026-01-30): if weak jobs data pull the front end lower, rate-sensitive REITs are the first to squeeze.

Narrative: Utilities have the demand but not the politics: XLU rose 1.31% over 20 sessions while CEG fell 20.55% and NEE rose 9.49% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-01-30). NERC forecasts peak demand up 24% on data-centre loads.

Reported: The read-across came from suppliers: GE Vernova's gas-turbine orders surged 74%, so new generation is booked years out and incumbents with existing plants hold the scarce asset. The market is not yet paying merchant nuclear for that scarcity: CEG fell 2.36% in the prior session (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-01-30).

EPS Upside Watch: Regulated utilities with contracted data-centre load: NEE's 9.49% gain against a 1.85% drop for merchant generator VST over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-01-30) shows the market paying for rate-base growth over power-price exposure that politics may cap.
⚡ Breaking Convention: Utilities want $31 billion more from customers — affordability, not demand, is now the binding constraint. Prefer regulated wires over merchant power.

Narrative: European autos are losing on three fronts: Chinese brands now make one in 10 cars sold in Europe, the euro's run toward $1.20 hurts exporters, and price wars squeeze margins. The SXAP tracker fell 6.24% over 20 sessions, BMW 9.24%, Mercedes 6.68% and Renault 12.32% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-01-30).

Reported: The read-across from Detroit was positive — GM hit an all-time high on results and a buyback — but it came from US trucks and capital returns that European makers cannot copy. VW's US ADR fell 2.42% in the prior session (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-01-30).

EPS Upside Watch: Stellantis is the cheapest restructuring option: STLA rose 1.33% over five sessions despite a 9.37% 20-session drop (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-01-30). With no fresh catalyst in the feed, upside depends on a European volume recovery.

⚡ Breaking Convention: Volkswagen held up best — VOW3 is down only 3.57% over 20 sessions versus 9.24% for BMW (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-01-30). A mass-market maker is outlasting premium brands, the opposite of the usual quality preference in a downturn.

Narrative: Semis remain the AI hardware core: SOXX rose 14.99% over 20 sessions, with ASML up 33.01%, MU 45.36% and INTC 25.93%, despite a 4.11% drop in the prior session (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-01-30). Memory is the binding constraint — Samsung and SK Hynix warn the crunch will last until 2027.
Reported: ASML's record orders smashed estimates as AI spurs demand, while AMD fell on MI450-series delay rumours and lost 6.13% in the prior session (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-01-30).

EPS Upside Watch: Memory and lithography: a shortage expected to last until 2027 lets contract prices reset higher, and ASML's record orders lock in equipment revenue. MU and ASML carry the cleanest estimate upside, with TSM, up 8.78% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-01-30), next.

⚡ Breaking Convention: Nvidia is the laggard inside the boom, up only 2.48% over 20 sessions while AVGO fell 4.28% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-01-30). The money is flowing to scarcity — memory and lithography — not to the GPU and custom-chip leaders.

Rewarded: Companies showing AI spending already paying back, or selling scarce capacity: Meta jumped on its revenue forecast, IBM on its beat, Caterpillar on power-generation demand, and ASML on record orders. GM's all-time high on results and a buyback shows old-economy names with capital returns get paid too.

Punished: Capex without visible payback and anything AI could disrupt: Microsoft lost $357 billion of market value, and PLTR, ORCL and MSFT fell 17.53%, 15.56% and 11.03% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-01-30). Weak guidance was not forgiven — UnitedHealth plunged on its first revenue-drop forecast in nearly four decades — and P&G's revenue miss mattered even in a hot staples tape.

Pattern: The bar is relative. Meta was rewarded because a stronger revenue forecast came with its spending, while Microsoft's mix of slowing cloud growth and huge AI spending produced its steepest drop in nearly six years. Physical bottlenecks — memory, turbines, power gear — earn a premium, seat-based software a discount, and beats in stocks that ran hardest into the print get sold.

Attention into EPS: The busiest stretch of the season tests the same question: Palantir on Feb. 2, then Alphabet and Amazon, and Lilly alongside the jobs data. Alphabet must pair capex with cloud acceleration, Amazon needs AWS to justify its spending, and Palantir must prove it is not priced like SaaS; Reuters frames the week as a test for stocks after Microsoft's swoon.

Playbook: Buy beat-and-raise names on first-day weakness only when revenue guidance rose; fade beats where the stock ran into the print and where capex rises without revenue guidance. Pair long memory and lithography scarcity (MU, ASML) against seat-based software until renewals show AI attach, and stop the pair if MSFT reclaims 483.62, its close 20 sessions earlier (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-01-30).

Attention Gap: Global attention is on AI and the metals crash, but Beijing quietly shifted: it reportedly dropped the rules that sparked the property crisis and plans $29 billion of special bonds to recapitalise insurers. FXI fell 2.87% in the prior session while staying up 3.45% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-01-30) — investors still trade China as a tech story, not as a balance-sheet repair story.

Exposure & Risk: Express it through FXI (39.61) and ASHR (33.44) rather than single developers (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-01-30), adding Hong Kong-listed insurers as the direct policy beneficiaries. The risk is credit: Vanke warned its 2025 loss may have widened to $11.8 billion. Exit if official January home-price data show the decline accelerating.

Attention Gap: The yen and the election take the headlines, but the BOJ's January summary shows members debating the risk of being behind the curve on inflation. With USD/JPY at 153.16 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-01-30), a BOJ that worries about falling behind has room to keep hiking, and the direct beneficiary is bank net interest income.

Exposure & Risk: Express via MUFG, SMFG and Mizuho ADRs, funded from yen-sensitive exporters given USD/JPY's 2.28% fall over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-01-30). Risks: a hung election or a consumption-tax suspension that triggers a disorderly JGB selloff, and a BOJ that pauses if the yen keeps strengthening.

Market Context: Bitcoin's prior completed daily close was 76,974.45, down 2.09% on the day, 13.61% over five sessions and 15.59% over 20; ether closed at 2,267.96, down 24.96% over five sessions, and solana at 100.85, down 27.52% over 20 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-01). IBIT fell 6.33% and COIN 10.24% over five sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-01-30). The FT says bitcoin slid to its lowest level since the 2025 tariff shock.

New / Most Important: The selloff is macro: Warsh is read as hawkish, which hits the most liquidity-sensitive risk first, and liquidations topped $2.5 billion as bitcoin, ether and XRP plunged. Traders are betting billions on a drop below $75,000 and bailing on upside. MSTR still rose 4.55% in the prior session to 149.71 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-01-30), a sign retail treats the treasury companies as dip vehicles.

Playbook: Stay underweight. If $75,000 breaks, expect forced selling around leveraged treasury companies — do not use MSTR as a dip vehicle. Re-enter via IBIT, at 47.49 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-01-30), only after bitcoin holds above its prior completed daily close of 76,974.45 for a week (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-01) and dollar strength fades.

Rates & Dollar: The DXY rose 0.74% to 96.99 in the prior session but is down 1.31% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-01-30); the bounce came as traders priced a more hawkish Fed chair. The curve is bear-steepening — the 10Y is up 8 bps over 20 observations to 4.26% and the 30Y sits at 4.87% (US Treasury, prior close 2026-01-30) — while TLT is flat over 20 sessions at 87.13 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-01-30).

Credit Check: Credit is open and calm: HYG rose 0.61% and LQD 0.34% over 20 sessions to 81.12 and 110.57 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-01-30), and US high-grade bond sales topped $200 billion in a record yearly start.
